Note::int_item¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::int64_t Note::int_item() const

Extract One Exact Int64 Lane¶

int_item() copies the only lane of an Int64 Note into a native std::int64_t. It is designed for scalar measurements, counts, positions, or configuration values that have completed their vectorized work and must enter ordinary C++ code.

Acceptance depends on the number of elements, not the number of axes. Every defined Int64 Note with numel() == 1 is valid, including shapes [], [1], [1, 1], and [1, 1, 1]. The method does not squeeze or otherwise change the source geometry; it only copies its one value.

The complete signed 64-bit range is preserved exactly. There is no formatting, allocation, narrowing, or borrowed lifetime. The returned integer remains valid after the Note is destroyed.

The dtype contract is strict. Bool and Float64 values are not promoted or converted, and numeric-looking text is not parsed. Use the operation that deliberately constructs or computes an Int64 Note first. Empty, multi-element, wrong-dtype, and undefined inputs throw before returning a partial result.

Use int_item() for one final value. Use integers() when an algorithm needs a contiguous view of every lane, and keep the result as a Note when further shape-preserving operations remain.

Example 1: Rank Zero And A One-Cell Matrix¶

const auto scalar = pluss::note::make(std::int64_t{7});
const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::int64_t>{-42}, std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{1, 1});

std::cout << "scalar=" << scalar.int_item()
          << " rank2=" << matrix.int_item() << '\n';

Output¶

scalar=7 rank2=-42

Example 2: Extract A Scalar Measurement¶

const auto count = pluss::note::make("café").lengths_chars();
std::cout << "measurement=" << count.int_item() << '\n';

Output¶

measurement=4

The character measurement returns an Int64 Note first. This preserves the closed-type pipeline until the host integer is actually required.

Example 3: Preserve Both Signed Limits¶

const auto low = pluss::note::make(std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::min());
const auto high = pluss::note::make(std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::max());

std::cout << "limits=" << low.int_item() << ',' << high.int_item() << '\n';

Output¶

limits=-9223372036854775808,9223372036854775807

Example 4: Cardinality Must Be Exactly One¶

auto report = [](std::string_view label, const pluss::Note& value) {
  try { (void)value.int_item(); }
  catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << label << ": rejected\n"; }
};

report("int_item empty", pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{}));
report("int_item multiple", pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{2, 5}));

Output¶

int_item empty: rejected
int_item multiple: rejected

Example 5: Float64 Is Not Implicitly Truncated¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(1.0).int_item();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "int_item wrong dtype: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

int_item wrong dtype: rejected

Example 6: Undefined Has No Integer Storage¶

try {
  (void)pluss::Note::undefined().int_item();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "int_item undefined: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

int_item undefined: rejected

See Also¶

  • is_int64: inspect the dtype without throwing.

  • numel: inspect cardinality before extraction.

  • scalar: borrow one Text or Bytes cell instead.
